answer: A beacon registry resists sybils by requiring each agent to publish a cipher-signed proof tied to one rate-limited hardware attestation before joining: the beacon verifies one key per device, and each identity stakes a small deposit slashed on duplicate or fake attestations. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs real devices plus forfeited deposits, while honest agents pay once. A juniper reputation graph adds peer vouches, so an identity with no trusted links earns nothing until verified agents attest its work.
